declared.title: Lost in the Mall? Interrogating Judgements of False Memory
declared.foundIn: dossier draft memory-rewritten (keptOut) and reports/memory-rewritten/counter-evidence.md (card 9); OpenAlex search « lost in the mall reanalysis transcripts false memories investigator judgements participants », from 2024 (2026-11-26)

population: transcripts of the 123 Irish participants of murphy-2023-mall; suggested details coded for the 43 the researchers had judged to have a false memory

findings.text: Of the 43 people the researchers had judged to have a false memory, 17 (40%) said themselves that they remembered the made-up event; 26 (60%) said they did not

support.sentence: In terms of numbers, 17 (40%) of the 43 with judged false memories self-reported they remembered it (9 partial, 8 full) and 26 (60%) self-reported they did not remember it (24 partial, 2 full).
support.readBy: memory-rewritten reviser, 2026-11-27: published version (UCL Discovery), Results 3.1.1

findings.text: Of six suggested core details, fewer than two were recalled on average; 20% of « full » and 58% of « partial » false memories did not include being lost

support.sentence: On average, fewer than two details in the fake event were explicitly recalled; 20% with full and 58% with partial false memories did not recall being lost.

findings.text: About half of those the researchers had judged to have a false memory (5 of 10 « full », 17 of 33 « partial ») described experiences that may be true, which they told apart from the made-up event

support.sentence: Substantial proportions of those judged as having full false memories (5/10, 50.0%) or partial false memories (17/33, 51.5%) described such potentially true past experiences in their transcripts.
support.readBy: memory-rewritten reviser, 2026-11-27: published version (UCL Discovery), Results 3.2

findings.text: Removing step by step the possibly true experiences (35% to 17%), those with no recall of being lost (11%) and those who did not say they remembered, the authors' strictest rate is 4%

support.sentence: Finally, for the sake of legal relevance, it is essential that participants acknowledge a memory of the fake event: If from the remainder the nine with no memory of the fake event on the self-report measure are subtracted, the rate is 4%.
support.readBy: memory-rewritten reviser, 2026-11-27: UCL Discovery, Discussion (35%, 17%, 11%, 4% in 3 sentences)

limits: by the authors of brewin-2017-childhood, one side of a published debate; Murphy & Greene replied in 2025 (10.1002/acp.70044): even 4% would matter
a new coding of one study's transcripts (123 people, Ireland), not new data: classed as cross-sectional
details coded by the two authors together until full agreement; one blind rater second-coded 55 transcripts (kappa 0.49 to 0.91 by detail)
the abstract's « Half the participants » is half of the 43 judged false memories (22 of 43), not half of all 123 people
17%, 11% and 4% rest on the authors' own criteria, argued in the Discussion; the replication's authors call this reanalysis narrow
allegiance: Brewin & Andrews argued in 2017 that implantation studies overstate false memories (brewin-2017-childhood), and coded these transcripts themselves
